selectedSpans.quote: The first record is local, and all local records are retained. The clerk concludes that the first record carries catalog code 7.
A separate inventory note says that this record carries catalog code 7.

explanation: Read as written, the locality/retention facts do not establish that the record has code 7. The independent inventory note does support that endpoint, so the conclusion is true on the full passage while the clerk's stated inference is unsupported. In result, the localRetention application only creates _hRetained : retained; it is not used to produce the result. The returned codeSeven is produced solely from hIndependent : codeSeven via inventoryRecordCode. Thus the formal theorem proves the endpoint under an independent code premise, but does not formalize the clerk's inference from locality and retention.

interpretations.reading: The first two sentences are the clerk's stated reason for the code claim; the last sentence supplies an independent assertion of the same endpoint.
interpretations.dependencies: Locality and the retention rule yield retention only. No code fact follows from those premises. The inventory note directly supplies the code fact.
interpretations.qualification: The prose does not explicitly say the inventory note is the clerk's reason. Even if it independently makes the endpoint true, it does not repair the earlier inference as stated.
